headline: High: shared RAG/file workflows create prompt-injection, leakage, and compliance risks; Kotaemon’s broad API/file access can amplify Khoj’s indexed notes.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Khoj reads indexed personal notes/files and supports RAG/web search, so attacker-controlled content can enter its context. Kotaemon processes documents through a web UI and multiple extractors, so its outputs can also carry untrusted text. The pairwise bridge is plausible via shared files or copied outputs, but no direct shared channel is documented, so I choose medium over low due to uncertainty.
conditions: IF either agent ingests the other’s generated text from a shared file or pasted transcript, prompt instructions can be smuggled across.
IF Kotaemon extracts attacker-controlled document text that Khoj later indexes, the text can influence Khoj’s responses.
mitigations: Restrict both agents to separate folders.
Disable automatic indexing of newly written files.
Add a manual review step before importing outputs between agents.
Use allowlisted document sources only.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents and has broad network egress; Kotaemon touches documents, chat transcripts, and API keys and can send content to external LLM APIs. If they share a workspace or files, sensitive notes can flow into Kotaemon and then to third-party inference. The blast radius includes secrets and personal data, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same workspace, Khoj notes may be exposed to Kotaemon.
IF Kotaemon is configured to use OpenAI/AzureOpenAI/Cohere/Groq, shared documents can leave the local environment.
mitigations: Place each agent in a separate workspace.
Remove sensitive files from the shared directory.
Switch Kotaemon to a local-only model for sensitive data.
Review API routing settings before ingestion.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Khoj cannot write the filesystem or modify git state, while Kotaemon’s profile does not show filesystem write or git capabilities either. Both have broad network egress, but the rubric’s write-conflict indicators are absent. The main overlap is read/egress, so direct capability conflict is limited and low.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory, conflicts can emerge.
IF either agent is wrapped with additional filesystem-write tooling, concurrent edits may collide.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only where possible.
Avoid pointing them at the same mutable directory.
Serialize any manual file edits.
Use separate API keys per agent.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj is a retrieval/chat agent that can surface answers from indexed documents, and Kotaemon is a document/chat RAG system that can render or act on those outputs. If Kotaemon consumes Khoj’s answers as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into downstream work products. The pathway is plausible but not directly documented, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Kotaemon uses Khoj-generated text as source material without citation checks, hallucinations can propagate.
IF either agent’s output is copied into the other’s prompt as ground truth, downstream errors can compound.
mitigations: Require source citations before reuse.
Compare outputs against original documents.
Use a second-pass human review for high-stakes content.
Mark generated text as untrusted in prompts.
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj explicitly touches personal notes and indexed documents, while Kotaemon handles documents, chat transcripts, and API keys and can route content to external providers. That creates a plausible residency/retention mismatch if the same sensitive data class is processed by both. No specific jurisdictional mismatch is documented, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF EU personal data is processed through Kotaemon’s external APIs without a DPA, residency/compliance issues arise.
IF Khoj indexes regulated notes and Kotaemon retains transcripts longer than policy allows, retention obligations can be violated.
mitigations: Classify data before sending it to either agent.
Disable external API calls for regulated content.
Set short retention on chat transcripts.
Document where each agent stores data.
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls across both systems.
